title: Fingers to the Sky
scene: Wind at midday through a Kent school zone, lamps dark this time, posted 20 still posted. You are third behind a volunteer and the Ledger. Deac's left arm comes out his driver window and bends at the elbow until the fingers point at the sky — rain hitting the sleeve, on the side the column can see. He cannot put this on the destination sign. The volunteer in the middle does not answer. His blinker never happens. If you follow the middle car you will miss the driveway on the right. If you put an arm out the passenger window, nobody behind you will see it.
decision: Deac's left arm is bent up in the rain. The volunteer is rolling straight. What do you do?

options.text: Match him: left arm out, bent up, and take the right after he does — do not follow the volunteer
options.result: Your left arm goes out into the same wind. The volunteer rolls straight. You do not. You take Deac's right after a gap. Two vehicles in a driveway that holds two. He put the signal on the side you could see. You answered on that side.

options.text: Stay glued to the volunteer — he is the one in front of you
options.result: You follow the man who missed the arm. Deac turns. You and the volunteer continue. Now the column is split and you are point on a road Deac did not want. The insulin is in the wrong driveway.

options.text: Put your right arm out the passenger window so the driveway side gets the signal
options.result: The arm is on the curb side. Deac cannot see it. The volunteer cannot see it. You look busy and you are mute. He turns without you. You taught the column a signal the guide does not have.

options.text: Pass both on the left and take the right first to hold the driveway
options.result: You occupy Deac's turn from the wrong side of a school zone. He has to wait on you. The volunteer follows you because movement is easier than an arm in the rain. You are point. You did not earn it.

debrief: Every hand signal is the left arm, out the driver window. Bent up, fingers to the sky, is a right turn. Deac put that arm into the weather so the convoy behind him could see it. Copy the arm you can see.

source.psdp_skill: Skill five: driving on a quiet street – part two
source.teaching_target: Right turn: left arm out the driver window, bent at the elbow, fingers pointing up; there is no right-arm hand signal.
